title: $p$-Body $\simeq$ Range $p-1$: Exact Order-Range Mapping and Dual-Unitarity
abstract: We introduce and study a periodically kicked version of a one-dimensional spin-$1/2$ Ising model with contiguous $p$-body interactions. At specific interaction strengths of the model, we establish an exact Floquet interaction $\textit{order-range}$ mapping: the Floquet evolution operator of the $p$-body Ising model is exactly mapped to a two body Ising model with interactions having maximum range $p-1$ and exactly determined couplings. Upon further tuning the kicking strength, the mapped model becomes dual-unitary, thus providing an explicit family of $p$-body dual unitary models. We then determine exact entanglement dynamics of the $p$-body model for a class of solvable initial states at all times. We further illustrate the nontrivial structures that can emerge from the $\textit{order-range}$ mapping using a minimal example of $p=3$ and generalize it for all odd $p$. These findings provide a systematic route to constructing and studying $p$-body dual-unitary Floquet models.
summary: This paper introduces an exact mathematical mapping showing that the dynamics of a $p$-body interacting Ising model can be simplified to an equivalent two-body model with a reduced interaction range. This 'order-range' duality provides a systematic method for constructing and studying solvable, dual-unitary Floquet quantum systems.
main_problem: The study focuses on understanding non-equilibrium dynamics of interacting quantum many-body systems, specifically extending concepts like dual unitarity to models with high-order $p$-body interactions.
main_result: The paper establishes an exact Floquet interaction order-range mapping, showing that the evolution of a $p$-body model can be mapped onto an equivalent two-body Ising model with maximum range $p-1$.
method: The authors use algebraic proofs involving Pauli matrices and induction to derive the mapping theorems, followed by analyzing spectral statistics and entanglement dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is a periodically kicked one-dimensional spin-$1/2$ Ising model featuring contiguous $p$-body interactions. The analysis focuses on the Floquet evolution operator derived from this Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Entanglement dynamics (e.g., $\alpha$-Rényi entropies) and spectral statistics (Poisson vs. Wigner-Dyson distributions).
important_parameters: Interaction strengths ($J=n\pi/4$), kicking strength ($b=\pi/4$), and the system size parity ($L$ even or odd).
main_assumptions: The mapping relies on specific tuning of interaction strengths (e.g., $J = n\pi/4$) and assumes periodic boundary conditions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate level spacing distributions for $p=3$, showing Poisson for even $L$ and Wigner-Dyson for odd $L$. Figure 3 shows the time evolution of 2-$	ext{Rényi}$ entanglement entropy for $p=3$ and $p=4$ under different initial state types.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops proofs (Lemma 2, Theorem 1) establishing the order-range mapping from $p$-body to $(p-1)$-range 2-body interactions. It then analyzes the consequences of this mapping based on the parity of system length $L$, concluding with entanglement dynamics calculations.
why_interesting: The explicit construction of dual-unitary models and the systematic reduction of high-order interactions into simpler, lower-dimensional effective Hamiltonians provide powerful tools for analyzing complex quantum many-body physics relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
